To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the first association between biallelic TTC21B pathogenic variants and heterotaxy.
biallelic TTC21B variants cause a spectrum of disease, and that the disease can manifest as heterotaxy.
biallelic TTC21B variants cause a novel ciliopathy syndrome with heterotaxy and other manifestations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genetic cause of a rare genetic disease, and the characterization of a novel heterotaxy syndrome.
the genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of congenital heart disease and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of congenital heart defects.

the identification of genes and genetic variants that cause human disease, with a particular focus on the identification of genes that cause congenital heart defects, and on the identification of novel genetic variants and genes that cause congenitally malformed hearts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this case demonstrates the association of heterotaxy and TTC21B variants, and that TTC21B is an important new heterozygous heterotaxy gene, with a potential role in situs determination.

the TTC21B gene encodes the protein, IFT139, which is a critical component of a retrograde transport system in the primary cilium and is associated with a broad spectrum of phenotypes, including focal segmental glomeulosclerosis, primary ciliary dysfunction, and situs abnormalities.
TTC21B is a novel heterotaxy‐associated gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TTC21B‐associated disease can be associated with heterotaxy, and that heterotaxy is a feature of the spectrum of TTC21B disease.
TTC21B‐associated disease can manifest with heterotaxy and/or situs inversus as well as other ciliopathy‐related phenotypes.

TTC21B is a novel heterotaxy‐causing gene, with a wide spectrum of clinical features, including focal segmental glomerosclerosis, and that the phenotypic overlap between ciliopathy‐associated and heterotaxy‐associated disease is likely to be more extensive than previously appreciated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phenotype of TTC‐21B spectrum disease is broad and includes heterotaxy.

TTC21B‐associated disease is not limited to classic ciliopathy phenotypes and should be considered in patients with focal segmental glucorulosclerosis, primary ciliary disease, biliary dysgenesis and/or heterotaxy, even without other features of a classic ciliopathy.
TTC21B should be considered in any child presenting with heterotaxy and a ciliopathy spectrum phenotype.
